title: claim_status='absent' is not proof of legacy provenance

spec.description: Treating claim_status='absent' as evidence that a row is legacy conflates 'no claim was recorded' with 'this predates the claim layer'. Those are different facts and the first does not imply the second.
spec.context: Durable fix per the review: a migration cutoff TIMESTAMP or an explicit allowlist, so legacy status is asserted from a recorded boundary rather than inferred from a missing value. Absence-as-evidence is the same reasoning error the declassified-records department names in its four-truth model. Cold independent review 2026-08-07, reviewer did not author either PR, read-only. PR#23 @ 3d648aa5c7f40551fa9137fd385ca81de0a15fd5 (re-fetched mid-review), PR#24 @ e3df51d4374cd79295e7af3c1529499bb2a52550. Both verdicts FIX-FIRST, neither RETHINK.
